turns.question: I'd love to hear about your coffee habits – think back to the last time you made a change with your coffee, whether that was trying a new brand, switching how you make it, or even just grabbing it from somewhere different than usual. What was going on that made you decide to do something different?
turns.response: I switched to buying from this place closer to my apartment a few months back instead of going to the chain I used to hit. Honestly it was just more convenient — I was tired of the detour, and their coffee's pretty good so there wasn't really a reason not to.

turns.question: What was happening on the days when you'd make that detour to the chain — what would that trip look like?
turns.response: I'd usually swing by on my way to work, like grab it before heading in. Nothing crazy — just pull up, order the same thing I always get, maybe wait a couple minutes if the line's longer than usual. In and out pretty quick. Sometimes if I had a morning meeting that was gonna be rough or I knew I'd be stuck at my desk all day I'd think "yeah I need the good coffee for this" and make sure to stop. But honestly most days it was just habit, not really a planned thing.

turns.focus_node_label: tired of making a detour for coffee

turns.question: Why does having that coffee stop be part of your morning routine feel important to you?
turns.response: I think it's just the one thing that's actually mine, you know? Like everything else in the morning is kind of on autopilot—getting ready, checking my phone—but the coffee is the one moment where I'm actually doing something deliberately. It wakes me up obviously, but it's more like... it gives the day a proper start instead of just stumbling into it.

turns.question: What happens on the mornings when you skip that coffee stop?
turns.response: Honestly, I'm usually pretty groggy until like mid-morning. I'll grab whatever's at home — instant coffee or just tea — but it's not the same. The whole routine kind of falls apart without it, so the day feels a bit off.
